question: Which filesystem security boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: a deny-wins `tools.fs` allow/deny policy, a `tools.fs.roots` access-mode policy, or a narrower workspace-only plus separate exec design?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and security boundary, and current open implementation candidates make different compatibility and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate boundary
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate security boundary with its own tracker.

options.title: Defer to OS or container isolation
options.body: Reject host filesystem path ACLs in OpenClaw core only if maintainers decide current workspaceOnly, sandbox backends, and operator OS controls are the supported boundary.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.
